newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes mostly lower, losses trimmed late.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes mostly lower, losses trimmed late.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mostly lower but losses were trimmed in late trade with featured late buyers including ADM and Cargill, traders said.
Pit sources said ADM bought 3.0 million bushels of May late and Cargill 700,000 bushels of May.
Talk that soybean acreage could be higher than previously expected, partly at the expense of corn, also contributed to the late advance.
"New crop (corn) caught hold pretty well on ideas that bean acreage is edging higher," analyst Bob Lekberg of Goldenberg-Hehmeyer said.

Dealers noted an Allendale-DTN survey issued Monday projected this year's U.S. corn plantings at 80.92 million acres while Refco Global Research forecast 80.0 million. Last year's planted area totalled 79.49 million, according to USDA.

Lekberg said early losses were mainly due to the market's overbought condition. He also said there was continued concern on the outlook for exports to Taiwan following the outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease among the island's hog herd.
"The Taiwan thing is still bothering people but the actual amount involved in cancellations in percentage terms of world trade is really pretty small," Lekberg said.
News that USDA had put weekly U.S. corn export inspections at 44.33 million bushels was supportive. Trade forecasts had ranged from 30.0 and 34.0 million.
Dealers said there was also talk China was temporarily halting corn exports although South Korea bought 49,000 tonnes of Chinese corn last Friday.
May corn closed 1-1/4 cents a bushel lower at $2.99 with other months down 1-1/2 cents to up 1-1/2. Volume on corn was estimated at 50,000 lots.
